newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle at $62, up $0.50-$1-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle at $62, up $0.50-$1-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle late Thursday traded briskly at $62.00, up $0.50-$1.00 from Wednesday, with most activity in Kansas, feedlot sources said.
About 13,000 head were reported sold in Kansas and about 300 in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area.
A few sales were reported earlier at $61.50 after midday, steady with Wednesday's top, the sources said.

Sales Wednesday were at $61.00, with a few at $61.50, sources said. Thursday's trade at $62.00 returned prices to the week's high established on Monday. However, the $62-price was down $1.00 from last week's top.
Sales were light in the Panhandle on Thursday as most showlists were sold out earlier in the week, sources said.
Week-to-date volume in the Panhandle near midday Thursday was estimated near 111,000 head, well above this week's showlist, which had been pegged about 103,000.
Kansas week-to-date sales late Thursday were near 90,000 head, which kept many feedlots fairly current, sources said.
With the showlists well sold, packers had to raise bids to extend inventories for next week, they said.
Fed cattle prices also were underpinned by strong beef movement so far this week, although packers had to lower prices to move beef out the door, several sources noted.
